Main.sentence: The University of Nairobi ( uonbi or UoN ; ___E:Swahili U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swahili_language)___ : Chuo Kikuu cha Nairobi )  is a ___E:collegiate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College)___ ___E:research university U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_university)___ based in ___E:Nairobi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi)___ and is the largest ___E:university U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_universities_and_colleges_in_Kenya)___ in ___E:Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya)___ .

Although its history as an ___E:educational institution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Educational_institution)___ dates back to 1956, it did not become an independent university until 1970. During that year, the ___E:University of East Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_East_Africa)___ was split into three independent universities: the ___E:Makerere University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makerere_University)___ in ___E:Uganda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda)___ , the ___E:University of Dar es Salaam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Dar_es_Salaam)___ in ___E:Tanzania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania)___ , and the University of Nairobi in Kenya.

During the 2023 academic year, the university had 49,047 students, of whom 35,897 were ___E:undergraduates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undergraduates)___ and 11,003 were ___E:postgraduates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postgraduates)___ .

The university launched several policy frameworks and introduced self-funded enrollment (also called 'module 2') to cope with the rising demand for ___E:higher education in Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_education_in_Kenya)___ .

The inception of the University of Nairobi dates back to 1956, with the establishment of the Royal Technical College, which admitted its first group of ___E:A-level U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-level)___ graduates for technical courses in April of the same year. The Royal Technical College was transformed into the second university college in ___E:East Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa)___ on 25 June 1961 by the Scottish mathematician Professor ___E:James Morton Hyslop U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Morton_Hyslop)___ ,  formerly of the ___E:University of Witwatersrand U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Witwatersrand)___ under the name Royal College of Nairobi.

It joined the ___E:University of London U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_London)___ 's ___E:'schemes of special relations' U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_London#Colleges_in_special_relation)___ and began preparing students in the faculties of ___E:Arts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arts)___ , ___E:Science U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science)___ and ___E:Engineering U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineering)___ for University of London award degrees.

Meanwhile, students in other faculties such as the Faculty of Special Professional Studies (later renamed Faculty of Commerce) and Faculty of ___E:Architecture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Architecture)___ continued to offer diplomas for qualifications of professional bodies/institutions.

On 20 May 1964, the Royal College of Nairobi was renamed University College Nairobi as a ___E:constituent college U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constituent_college)___ of the Federal University of East Africa.

During this time, enrolled students studied for college degrees awarded by the ___E:University of East Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_East_Africa)___ instead of the University of London.

In 1970, it transformed into the first ___E:national university U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_university)___ in ___E:Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya)___ and was renamed the University of Nairobi.
The university tops in Kenya's ___E:university ranking U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_ranking)___ .

It is ranked 7th in ___E:Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa)___ and 1698 in the world according to ___E:Webometrics Ranking of World Universities U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Webometrics_Ranking_of_World_Universities)___ . [citation needed]

The idea of an institution for higher learning in ___E:Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya)___ goes back to 1947 when the ___E:Kenyan colonial government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Colony)___ drew up a plan for the establishment of a technical and commercial institute in Nairobi.
By 1949, this plan had grown into a concept aimed at providing higher technical education for Kenya.
In September 1951, a Royal Charter was issued to the Royal Technical College, Nairobi and the foundation stone of the ___E:college U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College)___ was laid in April 1952.

During the same period, the ___E:Asian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_Asians)___ community was also planning to build a college for ___E:Arts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arts)___ , ___E:Science U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science)___ and ___E:Commerce U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commerce)___ as a memorial to ___E:Mahatma Gandhi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahatma_Gandhi)___ .
To avoid duplication of efforts, Gandhi Memorial Academy Society partnered with the colonial government.

Thus, the Gandhi Memorial Academy was incorporated into the Royal Technical College, ___E:Nairobi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi)___ in April 1954, and the college proceeded to open its doors to the first intake of students in April 1956.
Soon after the arrival of students at the college, the pattern of higher education in Kenya came under scrutiny.

Through the recommendation of a working party formed in 1958, chaired by the ___E:Vice-Chancellor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice-Chancellor)___ of the ___E:University of London U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_London)___ , Sir John Lockwood, the Royal Technical College, Nairobi was transformed.
On 25 June 1961, the college became the second ___E:university college U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_college)___ in East Africa, under the name "Royal College Nairobi."

The Royal College Nairobi was renamed "University College, Nairobi" on 20 May 1964. On the attainment of "University College" status, the institution prepared students for ___E:bachelor's degrees U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor%27s_degrees)___ awarded by the ___E:University of London U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_London)___ , while also continuing to offer college diploma programmes.

The University College Nairobi provided educational opportunities in this capacity until 1966 when it began preparing students exclusively for degrees of the ___E:University of East Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_East_Africa)___ , with the exception of the Department of Domestic Science.

With effect from 1 July 1970, the University of East Africa was dissolved and the three African countries of Kenya, ___E:Uganda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda)___ and ___E:Tanzania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania)___ each had its own national universities.
This development saw the birth of the University of Nairobi set up by an ___E:Act of Parliament U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Act_of_Parliament)___ .
Since 1970, the university had grown from a faculty based university serving a student population of 2,768 to a college focused university serving over 68,000 students.

In 2001, the first ___E:Confucius Institute U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confucius_Institute)___ in Africa opened as a collaboration between University of Nairobi and ___E:Tianjin Normal University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tianjin_Normal_University)___ in China.  : 139
It is a body corporate established under the ___E:Universities Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universities_Act)___ 2012 of the Laws of Kenya and the Charter.

Through module II and III programmes, opportunity has been opened to thousands of ___E:Kenyans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyans)___ and foreigners especially from Sudan, on a paying basis, who meet university admission requirements, but who have not been able to access ___E:university education U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_education)___ due to restricted intake into the regular programmes that is determined by limited resource allocation by ___E:Government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government)___ .

In addition to the regular, evening and, weekend programmes, classes are conducted at the University's Extra-Mural Centres located at the country's county ___E:headquarters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headquarters)___ .

The university is admitting students to undertake courses in the proposed ___E:Koitalel Arap Samoei University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koitalel_Arap_Samoei_University)___ College for ___E:law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law)___ , ___E:business management U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_management)___ and ___E:education U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education)___ courses that began in January 2015. This is a joint project of the ___E:County Government of Nandi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Government_of_Nandi)___ and the University of Nairobi.
The university underwent a major restructuring in 1983, resulting in decentralization of the administration, by the creation of six colleges headed by principals.
Further, in 2021, the university was further restructured to faculties headed by Deans,  phasing out the colleges.
In 2023, Times Higher Education ranked the university within the 1201–1500 band globally.
